units.function: HTTP route tests for reading and creating an instance-wide execution-environment catalog through company-addressed endpoints, including board authority, Secret envVar handling and activity fan-out.
units.dependencyDirection: Supertest/Vitest -> Express environment routes and real error middleware -> mocked environment, instance-settings, Secret, custom-image, workspace and activity services; database transaction behavior is replaced by a pass-through function.
units.keyDataModels: Instance-scoped environment catalog entry, board/Agent actor and company memberships, instance-admin flag, Secret-ref envVars and instance target, company-specific binding and per-company activity record.
units.lifecycle: Authorize company board access -> list shared instance environments or require instance admin -> normalize envVars in one company context -> create shared environment and replace instance Secret references -> sync requesting-company bindings -> emit activity to every company -> expose full config only to admin.
units.testAssessment: The approved unsandboxed focused run passed 7/7; the sandbox run failed 7/7 only because local listen was denied. Tests establish intended actor gates and service calls but cannot prove transactionality, Secret tenant isolation, activity durability, later-company behavior, concurrent creation or actual runtime authorization because all stateful services are mocked.
units.designRationale: Treat execution infrastructure as an installation-level resource managed once by an operator while allowing every company in that installation to select from the same catalog and receive change visibility.
units.companyOsProblem: Company OS needs deployment/node catalogs usable by both single-enterprise self-hosting and managed cloud without confusing infrastructure ownership, organization authorization, Connector capabilities or tenant-specific Secret/data bindings.
units.companyOsFit: REIMPLEMENT the scope model: separate deployment/node definitions owned by an operator from tenant-scoped execution profiles and explicit grants/bindings. A self-hosted profile may default one deployment to one enterprise; managed cloud must enforce tenant isolation. Preserve pre-read Agent denial and Secret normalization, but use structured errors, transactional outbox audit and per-tenant Secret references.
units.responsibilityConflict: Instance-admin authority and activity fan-out do not identify the accountable human or approved change contract. A shared environment mutation can affect every company's future Agent work, while the test binds Secrets only through one requesting company and provides no cross-company acceptance or revocation evidence.
evidence: 2026-08-19 sandboxed focused Vitest: 0/7 passed because local listen was denied (EPERM)
units.securityFindings: CRITICAL scope ambiguity for managed cloud: instance-wide environments are readable across companies while Secret normalization/binding originates from one company context. HIGH blast-radius gap: one instance admin mutates infrastructure used by every company without company acceptance/approval. HIGH transaction/audit gap: mocks do not prove atomic environment, Secret-reference, binding and multi-company activity writes. MEDIUM API-contract gap: company-nested paths address instance resources and tests rely on English error strings.
